prompt:
Spacious pastoral synthwave at 104 BPM in D minor, 4/4, half-time drums and long empty bars; the same
idea read as a chamber piece rather than a rock chorus.
Instrumentation: detuned saw pad carrying the harmonic bed, arpeggiated lead, round sub bass, gated
snare held to half-time, down-tuned rhythm guitars entering once in the chorus only.
Vocal: low male baritone, almost whispered in the verses, doubled at the octave in the chorus.
Theme: waking among valley orchids and birdsong with a stream below — the stream is the arpeggio, the
birdsong a filtered lead motif; no orchestral strings.
Production: tape-warm and spacious, narrow verses, chorus opens wide without distortion build-up.
Avoid: falsetto, orchestral strings, long ambient introduction, double-kick metal drumming, festival supersaws, EDM risers, distorted djent guitars, modern trap percussion
[0:00] Intro — pad bed and a stream-like filtered texture, no drums for four bars
[0:18] Verse 1 — baritone almost whispered, arpeggiated lead only, no guitars
[0:52] Chorus — down-tuned guitars enter once, pad opens wide, half-time drums
[1:20] Verse 2 — dry vocal over sub bass and pad, drums drop out for two bars
[1:48] Chorus — full but restrained, harmony stack on the hook, no distortion build-up
[2:12] Outro — chamber resolve on the pad and the stream motif, no fade
